{{EpicodePrevNext |prevcode=EP007 |prevtitle=The Water Flowers of Cerulean City |nextcode=EP009 |nexttitle=The School of Hard Knocks |series=original series |colorscheme=Kanto }} {{EpisodeInfobox |epcode=EP008 |colorscheme=Kanto |title_en=The Path to the Pokémon League |title_ja=ポケモンリーグへのみち |title_ja_trans=The Road to the Pokémon League |screen=hd |broadcast_jp=May 20, 1997 |broadcast_us=September 17, 1998 |en_series=Indigo League |en_op=[[Pokémon Theme]] |ja_op=[[Aim to Be a Pokémon Master|めざせポケモンマスター]] |ja_ed=[[One Hundred Fifty-One|ひゃくごじゅういち]] |olmteam=Team Ota |scenario=冨岡淳広 |storyboard=鈴木敏明 |director=鈴木敏明 |art=志村隆行 |morecredits=yes |epstaffpage=EP001-EP010 |footnotes=* {{filb-eppics|pm|008}} * ''[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rcA8dMGOMCw The Path to the Pokémon League]'' on the official [[Pokémon TV]] [[YouTube]] channel }} '''The Path to the Pokémon League''' (Japanese: '''ポケモンリーグへのみち''' ''The Road to the Pokémon League'') is the eighth episode of the [[Pokémon animated series]]. It first aired in Japan on May 20, 1997, and in the United States on September 17, 1998. {{spoilers}} ==Blurb== On the way to Vermillion{{sic}} City, Ash meets AJ, a Gym Leader at an unsanctioned Gym who has 98 wins and zero losses. They battle, and Ash is surprised that AJ's Ground-type Sandshrew can easily beat his Flying-type Pokémon. (Flying-type Pokémon are usually strong against Ground-type Pokémon.) Ash and his friends later see that AJ puts his Pokémon through very tough training—he makes his Sandshrew, normally weak to Water-type attacks, train in a swimming pool! Although Ash doesn't approve of the intensive training session, Brock is impressed. Ash begs for a rematch, but AJ refuses. The two argue a bit and when they fall into the pool, AJ's Sandshrew goes missing. Are AJ's training methods too tough? Will Ash get his rematch? And what happened to AJ's Sandshrew? ==Plot== ;Ash VS Savage Trainer A.J. {{Ash}} and {{ashfr}} are on their way to [[Vermilion City]]. Along the way, Ash has a {{pkmn|battle}} with another {{pkmn|Trainer}}, and {{AP|Pidgeotto}} defeats a {{p|Rattata}}, securing his tenth victory. The Trainer admires Ash's two Badges, leading {{an|Misty}} to muse that [[EP007|giving]] Ash the Badge may have been a mistake. The Trainer points Ash to an unofficial [[Gym]], where a strong Trainer named [[A.J.]], who has purportedly never lost a match, trains savage {{OBP|Pokémon|species}}. The sign outside A.J.'s Gym indicates that the Gym is unlicensed by the [[Pokémon League]] and that he has a record of 98 wins to zero losses. As Misty insults Ash, A.J. walks up and challenges him to a battle. A.J. snaps a whip, making Ash jump. He says that he plans to start competing for Badges after his 100th consecutive win. Ash smugly tells him that he has ten wins and two Gym Badges, at which point A.J. insults the Gyms, angering Misty and {{an|Brock}}. A.J. summons his {{p|Sandshrew}} to battle against Ash's Pokémon. Misty reminds Ash that Pikachu's electricity is [[Type#Type effectiveness|useless]] against a {{t|Ground}} Pokémon, but Ash rejects her advice. He summons Pidgeotto to battle Sandshrew. Brock notes that a {{t|Flying}} Pokémon should have the advantage. However, Sandshrew uses {{m|Defense Curl}} to roll up into a ball and hurls itself into the air, striking and [[Fainting|defeating]] Pidgeotto. After [[recall]]ing Pidgeotto into its {{i|Poké Ball}}, Ash calls out {{AP|Butterfree}} to fight Sandshrew. He orders a {{m|Stun Spore}} attack, but A.J., with a crack of his whip, orders Sandshrew to {{m|Dig}} underground to avoid it. It bursts out of the ground, taking Butterfree down as well. Ash wants Pikachu to fight next, but the {{pkmn|category|Mouse Pokémon}} refuses, grabbing hold of the edge of the battlefield. Ash tries to pull Pikachu off by the tail, but Pikachu, refusing to let go, hits his Trainer with a {{m|Thunder Shock}}. ;A.J.'s Harsh Training Methods While all of this is happening, {{TRT}} is spying on the match from a tree nearby and decides to steal Sandshrew. Refusing to believe that anyone's Pokémon could be so strong, Ash accuses A.J. of cheating and demands a [[rematch]], but A.J. tells him to quit whining. Later, Ash overhears A.J. {{pkmn|training}} his Pokémon, yelling angrily and cracking his whip. Ash intervenes to stop A.J. from hurting the Pokémon, but A.J. tells him to mind his own business. His Sandshrew is wearing a strength intensifier brace invented by A.J. himself. It enables the Sandshrew to withstand the weakening effects of water. A.J. says he's tougher on Sandshrew than his other Pokémon because it was his very first. Appalled at A.J.'s training methods, Ash asserts that a great Pokémon Trainer should make friends with his Pokémon. He asks for Brock's input, but Brock only wants to know what kind of {{pkmn|food}} A.J. is using. A.J., like Brock, mixes his own food from a secret recipe. Pikachu attempts to pick up one of Sandshrew's dumbbells, but falls backward under the weight, while Sandshrew does rapid exercises. Meanwhile, Team Rocket is crouched behind A.J.'s tent, preparing for their attempted heist. After the training, A.J.'s Pokémon are all exhausted. ;Team Rocket Snatches Up A Sandshrew A.J. insults Pikachu, and Ash takes a swing at him, causing them both to fall into the pool. Pikachu tries on the strength intensifier, but it fits badly and pulls him into a ball. Sandshrew laughs at Pikachu's comical appearance and rolls itself into a ball as well. Team Rocket rolls into the tent inside a rubber ball, intending to steal Pikachu, but they instead grab Sandshrew. After A.J. ends the rest break, he realizes that Sandshrew is missing. He releases Pikachu from the harness, but Pikachu doesn't know where Sandshrew is either. Ash suggests that it ran away because it saw that Pikachu was treated better. A.J. is extremely insulted at this, insisting Sandshrew would not have run away after all they had been through together. He sends his other Pokémon to look for Sandshrew, but Ash tries to convince A.J.'s Pokémon to leave with him. Despite the way A.J. has treated them, they ignore Ash. Meanwhile, while arguing over who carries the bag, Team Rocket is startled when Sandshrew flies out. Meowth {{m|Bite}}s Sandshrew's tail and Sandshrew burrows underground in pain. While Ash and A.J. are still arguing, Sandshrew bursts out of the ground next to him, dragging Meowth. Seeing how happy A.J. and Sandshrew are to be back together, Ash and the gang realize how deeply A.J. cares for his Pokémon. Surrounded by angry Pokémon and their Trainers, Meowth tries to figure a way out of his situation, when James and Jessie begin their {{motto}}. Jessie tells A.J. that taking his Sandshrew was a mistake; James calls it second-rate, earning A.J's ire. ;A.J.'s 100th Win? He challenges them to a battle, with his Sandshrew facing off against {{TP|Jessie|Ekans}} and {{TP|James|Koffing}}. Sandshrew avoids Koffing and Ekans's respective {{m|Sludge}} and {{m|Wrap}} attacks and takes them out, then defeats Meowth, who tries to Bite its armored skin. Team Rocket flees after Sandshrew's {{m|Fissure}} attack. As this is A.J.'s 100th win, he and his Pokémon now leave to begin earning Badges. Like Ash, he too wants to be the {{pkmn|world}}'s greatest [[Pokémon Master]]. They part as friendly rivals, agreeing to meet in the future at one of the League competitions. ==Major events== * {{Ash}} learns that there is [[Vermilion Gym|a Gym]] in [[Vermilion City]]. * [[Jessie's Ekans]] is revealed to know {{m|Wrap}}. * {{MTR}} is revealed to know {{m|Bite}}. {{animeevents|OS}} ===Debuts=== ====Pokémon debuts==== ==Characters== ===Humans=== [[File:Dare da EP008.png|thumb|200px|{{tt|Dare da?|Who's That Pokémon?}}]] * {{Ash}} * {{an|Misty}} * {{an|Brock}} * [[Jessie]] * [[James]] * [[A.J.]] * Trainer ===Pokémon=== [[File:WTP EP008.png|thumb|200px|Who's That Pokémon?]] [[Who's That Pokémon?]]: {{p|Sandshrew}} * {{p|Pikachu}} ({{OP|Ash|Pikachu}}) * {{p|Meowth}} ({{TRM}}) * {{p|Butterfree}} ({{OP|Ash|Butterfree}}) * {{p|Pidgeotto}} ({{OP|Ash|Pidgeotto}}) * {{p|Ekans}} ({{OP|Jessie|Ekans}}) * {{p|Koffing}} ({{OP|James|Koffing}}) * {{p|Sandshrew}} ([[A.J.]]'s) * {{p|Butterfree}} ([[A.J.]]'s) * {{p|Beedrill}} ([[A.J.]]'s) * {{p|Rattata}} ([[A.J.]]'s; ×3) * {{p|Rattata}} (Trainer's) ==Trivia== * This is the first [[filler episode|"filler" episode]] of the {{pkmn|animated series}}. * This is also the first episode without any {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} debuts. * This episode is the last in which [[Ted Lewis]] voices [[James]], as well as [[Eric Stuart]]'s first episode voicing James. He takes over the role when James summons {{p|Koffing}} in {{pkmn|battle}}. Lewis had left for a time to do theater, only to eventually return as {{an|Giovanni}} and {{Tracey}}. * This is the first episode not explicitly set within a location from the {{pkmn|games}}. * The English dub of this episode mentions a real animal. {{an|Misty}} claims that [[A.J.]] controls {{p|Sandshrew}} with the crack of his whip just like a {{wp|lion tamer}}. In the Japanese version, she simply remarks that it is amazing A.J. can control Sandshrew with the crack of his whip. * Early in the episode, {{TRT}} expresses an interest in Sandshrew. However, later on they say they take no interest in A.J.'s "second rate" Sandshrew. * This episode marks the first time that {{Ash}} has won a proper {{pkmn|Trainer}} battle onscreen. * This is the first episode where a [[one-hit knockout move]] is seen in the animated series. * Parts of this episode are remade in ''[[M20|I Choose You!]]''. * Ash's nose extending is a reference to the Japanese saying "Becoming a {{wp|Tengu}}", which is used to describe a person getting a swelled head. * This is the first episode where an unofficial Pokémon Gym is shown. * A.J.'s Sandshrew's strength intensifier resembles a [[Macho Brace]], an item that is not introduced until [[Generation III]]. ===Errors=== * [[Pokémon.com]]'s blurb for this episode misspells {{ci|Vermilion}} as Vermil'''l'''ion. * When Misty says that she and {{an|Brock}} giving {{Ash}} the [[Badge]]s was a mistake, the strap of her bag is the same color as her shirt. * When Ash and {{ashfr}} are standing in front of [[A.J.]]'s [[Gym]], Ash's sleeves are briefly colored blue instead of white. * When Ash and his friends turn to see A.J, Ash's left hand briefly overlaps {{an|Brock}}. * When A.J.'s {{p|Butterfree}} takes his bag, the straps on Ash's bag are colored black instead of green. * When Sandshrew dives into the pool, its eyes have their colors reversed. * When A.J.'s Sandshrew curls into a ball to be passed around by A.J.'s three Rattata, it is mistakenly drawn without its brace on. * When Team Rocket is sneaking around A.J.'s Gym while inside of a ball, {{MTR}}'s forepaws are colored orange instead of cream. * When A.J. is grateful when Sandshrew returns, his Butterfree's antennae disappear several times. * In this episode, A.J.'s Sandshrew uses {{m|Defense Curl}}. However, in the games, Sandshrew couldn't learn Defense Curl until [[Generation II]]. * In the English dub: ** When Ash tells A.J. that Sandshrew are weakened by water, he incorrectly says "[[List of nonstandard species plurals|Sandshrews]]." The plural of a specific species of Pokémon is the same as the singular. ** When Pikachu is holding a pillow, Ash's Japanese voice can be heard. EP008 error.png|Ash's miscolored straps EP008 error 3.png|Sandshrew's miscolored eyes EP008 error 2.png|Meowth's miscolored forepaw ===Dub edits=== * [[Kanto Pokérap]]: Day 3 * The sign over the [[Gym]] is heavily edited: ** The text is translated. ** The background changes from plain white to a gray that fades into white. ** The numbers are made into a dot-matrix format. In the original version, they were in a 7-segment LED format. ** The number of losses (0) is added. * A sign inside the tent saying "Fight! Work Harder!" is changed to a picture of a {{i|Poké Ball}} being hit with a whip. * The scene where {{AP|Pikachu}} holds a pillow is different between the two versions, due to the original Japanese version incorporating both an untranslatable pun and pop culture reference. In said original version, {{Ash}} tells [[A.J.]] that Sandshrew (whose Japanese name is "サンド (Sand)") is not a "サンドバッグ" (or "sandbag", which is the Japanese word for {{wp|punching bag}}), and Pikachu pulling out a ''{{wp|zabuton}}'' (a type of pillow) is a reference to the Japanese comedy program ''{{wp|Shōten}}'', where participants are awarded with ''zabuton'' for giving humorous responses, causing Ash to shout at Pikachu for not taking him seriously. In the English dub, the script was rewritten to have Ash mishear A.J., thinking he said ''pacing'', not ''passing'', and Pikachu's pillow further stammers him into saying ''padding''. * {{TRT}} experiments with a different motto: ** Japanese: *** [[Jessie]]: "We are the pretty thieves..." *** [[James]]: "Target: Pikachu!" ** English dub: *** Jessie: "Team Rocket will do what it has to do..." *** James: "To snatch that little Pikachu!" * At the end, a five-second panning of the battle field is cut by three seconds and replaced by a three-second clip from earlier in the episode. * After defeating the Rattata trainer, Ash brags about the two badges he has. In the original version, Brock and Misty say that they were pity badges. In the dub, they say that maybe they made a mistake giving him the badges. * After bragging about his badges to A.J., in the original version A.J. asks what puny gyms Ash got his badges from. In the dub, he wonders if Ash got them from failure city or wimpsville. He also calls them loser gyms. * In the original version, while spying on everyone Meowth comments that James is full of himself when he hasn't caught Pikachu yet, before James hits him. In the dub, the reason James hits him is because Meowth says James looks like he's trick or treating unlike A.J. when talking about his looks. * In the original version, after Ash and A.J. fall in the water, Ash says that Sandshrew will die in the water. In the dub, Ash says that A.J. is hurting Sandshrew.
